title: GPU min/max + trigger gridsearch notes — Jun 2026
summary: Working notes and raw results from a targeted grid-search of min/max instance settings and trigger thresholds across three regions. Goal: find conservative min/max and trigger configs that reduce cost without degrading p95 latency beyond SLO (400ms) and keep average GPU utilization between 55–75%.
body:
Status: draft working doc (choppy notes). Purpose: bake a deployable min/max + trigger recommendation for the regional autoscaler by end of Q2. This doc collates short experiments run between 2026-06-10 and 2026-06-25 across us-west1, eu-central1, and ap-southeast1. Runs used production-like traces replayed against a staging fleet (same model variants as canary).

Key constraints and KPI targets:
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 400ms for request class A (chat generation).
- Cost target: reduce steady-state GPU spend vs baseline by >= 10% without violating latency SLO.
- Util target: 55–75% average GPU utilization during steady state.
- Max scale-up time target: <= 90s to add a new instance and reach steady throughput.

Quick summary of approach:
- Gridsearch knobs: min_instances (1,2,4), max_instances (8,12,20), scale_up_rps_threshold (8,12,18 req/s per instance), scale_up_gpu_util_threshold (60,70,80), cool_down (60s,90s,180s), warm_pool (on/off, warm_size 1–2).
- Each experiment ran for 6h: 2h ramp from 0 to peak (production replay), 2h sustained peak, 2h ramp down. Collected per-10s metrics: p50/p95 latency, token-per-second, GPU util, instances online, queue length, cold-start counts, and cost estimator outputs.

Experiment matrix (compact table; raw CSV attached in linked artifact above):

ID | min | max | up_trigger_rps | up_trigger_util% | cool_down_s | warm_pool | region | observed_p95_ms | avg_gpu_util% | cost_delta_vs_baseline | notes
E01 | 1 | 8  | 12 | 70 | 90  | on  | us-west1    | 365 | 58 | -4%  | baseline-ish, small savings, occasional p95 spikes during 1->2 transitions
E02 | 2 | 8  | 12 | 70 | 90  | on  | us-west1    | 345 | 63 | -9%  | smoother p95, better utilization, recommended candidate for low-traffic customers
E03 | 1 | 12 | 18 | 80 | 60  | off | eu-central1 | 410 | 49 | -12% | cost wins but violates p95 on sustained bursts -> not acceptable for class A
E04 | 4 | 20 | 12 | 60 | 180 | on | us-west1    | 330 | 69 | +1%  | higher baseline cost, very stable latency, good for high-throughput tenants
E05 | 1 | 8  | 8  | 60 | 90  | off | ap-southeast1 | 388 | 54 | -7% | conservative triggers keep util low but borderline cost
E06 | 2 | 12 | 12 | 70 | 90  | on  | eu-central1 | 355 | 61 | -10% | strong candidate: meets p95 and cost target in eu-central1 trace
E07 | 2 | 12 | 12 | 70 | 90  | on  | ap-southeast1 | 372 | 59 | -8% | similar to eu but slower scale-up due to pod startup latency in region
E08 | 1 | 20 | 18 | 80 | 60  | on  | us-west1    | 395 | 52 | -15% | large max allows cost reduction at exp risk; p95 close to SLO under extreme bursts

Notes on observed behaviors and cross-experiment patterns:
- Min instances has outsized impact on p95 during north-south traffic transitions. Going from min=1 to min=2 reduced transient p95 spikes by ~6–8% in the replayed traces. For multi-tenant production we should prefer min>=2 for shared endpoints.
- Warm pool dramatically improves scale-up tail (cold-starts reduced by ~65% in runs with warm_pool on). Warm pool cost overhead was ~+2–3% but frequently paid for itself by avoiding p95 violations that would require emergency fallback.
- Aggressive up_trigger (high rps/util thresholds) gives strong cost improvements but increases p95 risk during sudden sustained bursts. The sweet spot across traces was up_trigger_rps=12 and up_trigger_util=70%.
- Cool-down tuning: too short (60s) led to oscillation in a subset of traces (instances flapping 2->3->2). 90s was a reasonable compromise for traces used; 180s was safe but increased sustained cost.
- Regional differences: ap-southeast1 showed longer container startup times (observed 1.4x median cold start) — treat region-specific startup latencies as a first-class input to autoscaler configs. eu-central1 had the most stable runtime and best cost/latency balance.

Quantitative highlights (aggregate across repeats):
- Best candidate (E06 config: min=2,max=12,up_rps=12,util=70,cooldown=90,warm_pool=on) averaged p95=355ms, avg util=61%, cost -10% vs current baseline.
- Aggressive cost-first config (E08) hit cost -15% but p95 approached 395ms during synthetic step-bursts — too risky as global default. Might be acceptable as "cost-optimized" tier for non-latency-critical customers.
- Baseline configs with min=1 often required emergency fallback during blue-green deploys or irregular traffic spikes.

Actionable recommendations (short):
1) Default region profile: adopt E06-like profile as default for hosted-api production endpoints in eu/us regions: min_instances=2, max_instances=12, up_rps_threshold=12, up_util_threshold=70%, cool_down=90s, warm_pool=enabled (warm_size=1).
2) Conservative tier: for enterprise customers with stricter latency SLOs, recommend min=4, cool_down=180s, pre-warmed replica per-region. Accept higher cost (+~1–4%).
3) Cost tier: create an opt-in "cost-optimized" autoscaler policy (min=1,max=20, aggressive triggers) that customers can select or that internal batch workloads use. Annotate clearly that p95 risk is higher under sudden bursts.
4) Region overrides: add region-specific adjustments for ap-southeast1 (increase warm_pool size to 2 or bump min_instances by +1) until we reduce cold-start variance.
5) Monitoring: add synthetic probe that simulates a 2-min step-burst every 4h in staging to validate p95 headroom for any candidate policy before rollout.

Open questions and TODOs:
- Should we let max_instances remain large (20) for a cost-tier or cap at 12 for default? Operational risk vs headroom tradeoff — need product input. (see INFRA-824)
- We used the same model variant for all runs; different larger models have different warm-up characteristics. Need a short run matrix for "m-xxl" family.
- Cost estimator needs an add-on for warm_pool sizing to model hot standby incremental cost. Current estimator undercounts standby GPU costs by ~10% in our runs.
- Follow-up experiment: try adaptive cool_down that increases after a scale-down event. Could reduce oscillation.

Appendix: rough run diary (notes to self):
- 2026-06-11: E01/E02 run. Observed a race condition in the scale-controller when multiple triggers hit simultaneously (ticketed, fixed in PR #412).
- 2026-06-13: E03 showed p95 > SLO in eu trace. Replayed with warm_pool on — p95 improved by ~22ms.
- 2026-06-18: E04 long-run (12h) to check oscillation; none observed but cost drift higher than expected.
- 2026-06-23: E06 repeated 3x for confidence; results stable.

Short checklist before promoting default policy to production:
- [ ] Run E06 profile against canary fleet for 48h with traffic mirroring for three representative endpoints.
- [ ] Add region override for ap-southeast1 with warm_pool size 2 and validate.
- [ ] Update cost estimator to reflect warm_pool steady-state overhead.
- [ ] Draft release notes and product comms for "default autoscaler refinement — Jun 2026".

Notes to reviewers: this doc is intentionally informal. Please add comments inline (or drop quick notes in INFRA-824). If you think the default max_instances=12 is too tight for expected holiday peaks, flag that in the ticket and we'll run a targeted high-peak sim.

-- Marcus

(attachments: raw csvs, Grafana dashboards snapshots, and the replay traces are linked in linked_artifacts -> INFRA-824)
